slides.caption: Red brought the stones to the bed, and the huntsman placed all six inside the wolf.
slides.action: Little Red Riding Hood goes to the accessible side of the bed, passing the clear central floor (standing beside the open belly, holding her emptied cape beneath the huntsman's hands). The Huntsman leaning over the bed, settling the sixth heavy stone inside the wolf, careful and determined.

slides.caption: The huntsman stitched the wolf closed with the threaded needle.
slides.action: The Huntsman drawing the threaded needle through the final stitch, satisfied but watchful. The Wolf still asleep on his back, with his stone-filled belly stitched closed.

slides.caption: The wolf woke and tried to flee, but the heavy stones dragged him down.
slides.action: The Wolf stands up at the accessible side of the bed (out of bed on buckling legs, pitching toward the door beneath his stone-filled belly).

slides.caption: The wolf fell dead beside the bed.
slides.action: The Wolf lies down at the open bedside floor (lying dead on the floor beside the bed, weighed down by his stone-filled belly).

slides.caption: Red hugged Grandmother tightly as they shared cake with their rescuer, and she promised never to stray from the path again.
slides.action: Little Red Riding Hood goes to the small wooden table, passing the open bedside floor (beside Grandmother at the table, hugging her tightly with one arm and offering cake from the basket with the other). The Huntsman leaning from the adjacent sewing shelf to take a bite of the cake Red offers, keeping his tools lowered, warmly relieved.
